bullets.title: MU: Citi sees 6% EPS upside; Aug-Q target $28+; DRAM ASPs +20% YoY
bullets.body: Citi models 6% EPS upside to MU's May-Q and expects $28+ EPS for the Aug-Q on DRAM ASPs 20%+ YoY vs. their 19% guidance. MU reports June 24 AH vs. consensus of $20.57 EPS / $35.56B revenue. Memory vendors broadly expected to positively comment on capex with upward bias at 2Q earnings; Samsung 2Q26 operating profit seen exceeding W100tr as DRAM/NAND prices track up 50-60% QoQ vs. original 20-30% forecast.

bullets.title: QCOM: Investor Day 6/24 — data center push, custom silicon ramping Dec 2026, PC target withdrawal
bullets.body: Qualcomm's June 24 Investor Day will highlight AI200/AI250 inference accelerators, server CPUs, and custom ASICs funded by fungible smartphone wafer capacity. A hyperscale customer (HUMAIN primary) is ramping a custom silicon LPU chip in December 2026 targeting 200MW. Citi/Jefferies expect QCOM to raise Automotive ($8B) and IoT ($14B) targets while withdrawing its $4B PC sales target by F29 due to memory constraints.

bullets.title: Backend switch market surging: CLS #1, CSCO gaining fast, NVDA losing share
bullets.body: Dell'Oro 1Q data: Ethernet backend switch market grew >100% YoY to >$3.7B; InfiniBand >200% YoY to >$2B. CLS holds #1 with >25% share (only vendor shipping early 1.6T in small volumes) but lost ~5 pts YoY. NVDA at 24% share, down 6 pts, planning Spectrum-X CPO shipments 2H. CSCO gained +8 pts to ~8% overall and ~13% within top 4 cloud customers, driven by Meta deployments. ANET gained +3 pts to 12%.

bullets.title: ACN: JPM maintains OW, cuts PT to $179 from $201; M&A offset to weak organic
bullets.body: Accenture's F3Q revenue of $18.72B slightly missed; FXN growth 3.1% vs. 3.2-3.6% consensus with geopolitical disruption costing ~$100M in consulting revenue and ~$400M in bookings. FY26 FXN guidance narrowed to +3-4%; FY27 implies ~1% organic growth. JPM cuts PT to $179 (11x CY28 EPS) from $201 but maintains OW, citing M&A track record ($9B raised) and EPS protection ($3.80 actual vs. $3.64-3.72 consensus). GS sales desk flags weaker bookings (-3% YoY) and large managed services deals slipping to FY27.

bullets.title: AMZN/AWS: Citi projects +37% FY27 revenue growth on agentic AI wave
bullets.body: Post-AWS NYC Summit, Citi reiterates AMZN as top Internet pick and projects AWS revenue growth accelerating to +37% YoY in FY27 vs. +30% FY26, driven by agentic AI productionization. AWS Bedrock AgentCore agent task volume is up 15x in six months. Separately, Amazon is in talks to sell custom AI chips to third-party data center customers, competing with Nvidia.

bullets.title: SNOW, MDB, ORCL: AI data infrastructure plays highlighted at AWS Summit and by Wolfe
bullets.body: Citi sees positive takeaways for SNOW, MDB, MSFT, and ORCL from AWS Summit with PoCs maturing to production. SNOW's Observe product shows triple-digit growth; ESTC eyeing 20-30% pricing increase as Platinum tier sunsets. Wolfe Research adds SNOW as public proxy for Databricks AI/data trends and sees MDB 2H AI tailwinds; ORCL benefiting from cloud migration acceleration via 26ai and vector workloads.

bullets.title: PLTR, NOW, TEAM, CRM: Wolfe sees agent wave benefiting enterprise platforms; PLTR valuation a ceiling
bullets.body: Wolfe's Zukin notes NOW, TEAM, and CRM as primary beneficiaries of the enterprise agent deployment wave; CRM's Agentforce/Intercom acquisition enhances capabilities. PLTR flagged as best product-market fit in software but valuation warrants only neutral stance. IONQ at 7x revenue for 24% growth cited as an attractive long entry.

bullets.title: META: lobbying for child-harm lawsuit immunity; 1.6GW compute from Crusoe; driving CSCO switch share
bullets.body: Meta is lobbying Congress for immunity from child-harm lawsuits. On infrastructure, Meta secured ~1.6GW AI compute from Crusoe (two Texas/Missouri facilities) and CPO-based 1.6T switching expected in 1H27. Meta's deployments are the primary driver behind CSCO's +8 pt backend switch share gain.

bullets.title: AAPL: chip deal with Intel; Brazil alternative app stores; price increases signal tight memory
bullets.body: Trump stated Apple agreed with Intel to design/manufacture chips in the US, diversifying from TSMC; Intel rose ~10% on unconfirmed reports. Apple also agreed to permit alternative marketplaces and external payments in Brazil following an antitrust settlement. Apple raising product prices due to rising component costs, reinforcing tight DRAM/NAND pricing environment.

bullets.title: MRVL: in talks with TSMC on A14 process for next-gen AI connectivity chips
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reports Marvell is in talks with TSMC to use the A14 node for next-generation AI connectivity chips, signaling continued positioning in high-bandwidth AI interconnect silicon.

bullets.title: NFLX: acquiring Radford Studio for ~$400M; expanding traditional broadcaster partnerships
bullets.body: Netflix is under contract to acquire Radford Studio Center for ~$400M, well below the 2021 $1.85B sale price. CEO confirmed strategy to add more traditional broadcasters to platform following the TF1 deal in France.

bullets.title: NVDA: losing backend switch share but ASML CEO bullish on multi-year AI chip supply constraint
bullets.body: NVDA fell to 24% backend switch share (down 6 pts YoY) with CPO Spectrum-X shipments planned 2H. On the positive side, the ASML CEO is bullish on a multi-year supply-limited AI chip market; ASML's 90-unit EUV guidance may be a floor with potential upside to 110-120 units per GS sales desk. EUV China headline risk characterized as sentiment overhang rather than fundamental threat.

bullets.title: HF positioning: gross leverage near peak; Tech net sold but Info Tech still top contributing sector
bullets.body: JPM prime data shows HF gross leverage at highs after a 22% May increase and 18% June increase — historically leverage peaks at mid-June options expiry before declining. HFs net sold US Tech and Industrials (strongest performers) while AI Vulnerable, Low End Consumer, and Med Tech remain sub-10th percentile in positioning. Russell rebalance is a near-term event risk with an unusually large estimated trade size.

bullets.title: Macro: Fed hawkish tilt — 9 members expect 2026 hikes; core PCE projection jumps to 3.3%
bullets.body: FOMC June dots show nine members expecting 2026 rate hikes with six looking for two or more moves; 2026 core PCE projection raised from 2.7% to 3.3%. Piper Sandler still sees S&P 500 reaching 8,450 at 21.5x on $393 2027 consensus EPS, driven by earnings growth not multiple expansion. Room for P/E expansion limited absent a sustained rate decline.

bullets.title: Oil: Iran deal execution risk; stranded supply recovery supports bearish crude, dovish rotation
bullets.body: Jefferies flags the US-Iran deal shifting from geopolitical risk pricing to execution credibility. Hormuz reopening could release ~165M barrels of stranded supply; IEA estimates 14M bpd was disrupted. Lower oil is disinflationary, supporting a dovish Fed read and rotation into consumer discretionary, travel, airlines, housing, and autos — and away from energy.
